title: US National Debt Reaches Historic $40 Trillion Milestone
subtitle: Rising government spending and high interest rates push the national debt to new, record-breaking levels.

summary.en: The United States national debt has officially surpassed $40 trillion for the first time in history. This massive figure reflects years of high government spending under both the Trump and Biden administrations. Experts warn that the current path of borrowing is unsustainable and could hurt the economy. High interest rates are making it more expensive for the government to pay back its loans. Meanwhile, Congress faces pressure to address the budget as the nation approaches a potential government shutdown.
summary.zh: 美國國債歷史上首次正式突破 40 兆美元。這個龐大的數字反映了川普與拜登政府多年來的高額支出。專家警告，目前的借貸路徑無法持續，可能會損害經濟。高利率使得政府償還貸款的成本變得更加昂貴。與此同時，隨著國家接近政府停擺的邊緣，國會正面臨解決預算問題的壓力。

paragraphs.en: The United States has reached a major economic milestone as its national debt climbed past $40 trillion. According to figures from the Treasury Department, this record-breaking number shows how quickly the government’s borrowing has grown over the last decade. In 2016, the national debt was just under $20 trillion, meaning it has more than doubled in only ten years.
paragraphs.zh: 美國達成了一項重大的經濟里程碑，其國債金額已突破 40 兆美元。根據財政部的數據，這個破紀錄的數字顯示出政府的借貸在過去十年中成長得有多快。2016 年時，國債金額還不到 20 兆美元，這意味著國債在短短十年內成長了一倍以上。

paragraphs.en: This rapid increase is the result of years of heavy government spending. Reports from The Guardian note that both the Donald Trump and Joe Biden administrations contributed to this total. During his first term, President Trump approved $8.4 trillion in debt, much of which was used for Covid-19 relief. President Biden later approved $4.3 trillion in debt. Today, the government spends more than a trillion dollars every year just to pay the interest on its existing loans. According to NPR, interest payments are now the second-largest expense for the federal government, behind only Social Security.
paragraphs.zh: 這種快速增長是政府多年來高額支出的結果。《衛報》(The Guardian) 的報導指出，川普 (Donald Trump) 與拜登 (Joe Biden) 兩任政府都對此總額有所影響。川普在第一任期內批准了 8.4 兆美元的債務，其中大部分用於新冠肺炎的紓困。拜登隨後則批准了 4.3 兆美元的債務。如今，政府每年僅支付現有貸款的利息就超過一兆美元。根據美國公共廣播電台 (NPR) 的報導，利息支出目前已成為聯邦政府第二大開銷，僅次於社會安全福利。

paragraphs.en: There are several reasons why the debt is growing so quickly. NPR reports that the government is currently spending more than $2 trillion more than it collects in tax revenue each year. Recently, the deficit—the difference between what the government spends and what it earns—grew even larger after the Supreme Court ordered the Treasury to refund over $100 billion in import taxes, known as tariffs, that were collected illegally. While government revenue has grown by 3% this year, spending has increased at a much faster rate.
paragraphs.zh: 國債成長如此迅速的原因有幾個。NPR 報導稱，政府目前的年度支出比稅收收入多出 2 兆美元以上。最近，赤字（即政府支出與收入之間的差額）在最高法院下令財政部退還超過 1,000 億美元非法徵收的進口稅（即關稅）後變得更加嚴重。雖然政府收入今年成長了 3%，但支出增加的速度卻快得多。

paragraphs.en: This situation has caused significant concern among financial experts. Maya MacGuineas, president of the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget, stated that this debt is not just a number on a government report. She explained that it affects the entire economy and the daily lives of citizens. As the government borrows more money, it can make inflation—the general rise in prices for goods and services—worse. It also makes it harder for the government to pay for other important programs.
paragraphs.zh: 這種情況引起了金融專家們的重大擔憂。聯邦預算責任委員會 (Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget) 主席瑪雅·麥吉尼斯 (Maya MacGuineas) 表示，這筆債務不僅僅是政府報告上的一個數字。她解釋說，這會影響整個經濟以及公民的日常生活。隨著政府借入更多資金，這可能會加劇通貨膨脹（即商品與服務價格的普遍上漲）。這也使得政府更難以負擔其他重要的計畫。

paragraphs.en: Rising interest rates have made the problem even more difficult. When the government borrows money, it issues bonds, which are essentially loans from investors. Investors now demand higher interest rates, known as yields, to lend money to the government. According to BBC Business, the interest rate on 30-year bonds recently reached its highest level in nearly 20 years. These high rates do not just affect the government; they also raise the cost of mortgages, car loans, and credit cards for regular people. For example, the average rate for a 30-year home loan has recently climbed toward 6.7%.
paragraphs.zh: 不斷上升的利率使問題變得更加棘手。當政府借錢時，會發行債券，這本質上就是向投資人貸款。投資人現在要求更高的利率（即殖利率）才願意借錢給政府。根據 BBC 商業新聞報導，30 年期債券的利率最近達到了近 20 年來的最高水準。這些高利率不僅影響政府，也提高了普通民眾的房貸、車貸和信用卡成本。例如，30 年期房屋貸款的平均利率最近已攀升至接近 6.7%。

paragraphs.en: In an attempt to lower these borrowing costs, the Treasury Department announced it would double its buyback operations. A buyback is when the government repurchases its own debt to help stabilize the bond market. While this move helped lower interest rates slightly, experts like John Canavan of Oxford Economics warn that it is unlikely to provide a long-term solution to the country’s debt problems.
paragraphs.zh: 為了試圖降低這些借貸成本，財政部宣布將加倍進行債券回購操作。回購是指政府買回自己的債務，以協助穩定債券市場。雖然此舉有助於稍微降低利率，但牛津經濟研究院 (Oxford Economics) 的約翰·卡納萬 (John Canavan) 等專家警告，這不太可能為國家的債務問題提供長期解決方案。

paragraphs.en: Political leaders remain divided on how to handle the situation. The White House has stated that it is focused on cutting waste and fraud in federal spending to improve the nation’s financial health. However, critics argue that there is no clear plan to stop the debt from growing. Carolyn Bourdeaux of the group Concord Action warned that the current situation should be a wake-up call for leaders in Washington. She noted that the country owes it to future generations to find a more responsible path.
paragraphs.zh: 政治領袖對於如何處理這種情況仍存在分歧。白宮表示，目前正致力於削減聯邦支出中的浪費與詐欺行為，以改善國家的財務健康。然而，批評者認為，目前並沒有明確的計畫來阻止債務繼續成長。康科德行動組織 (Concord Action) 的卡羅琳·伯多 (Carolyn Bourdeaux) 警告說，目前的情況應該是對華府領袖的警鐘。她指出，國家有責任為後代子孫找到一條更負責任的路。

paragraphs.en: As the government continues to borrow, it is also facing a deadline. Congress is currently working on a new spending bill to fund the government. If a deal is not reached by September 30, the federal government could face a shutdown, which would stop many public services. With the debt now at $40 trillion and the government nearing its legal borrowing limit, the pressure on lawmakers to find a solution is higher than ever.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著政府持續借貸，它也面臨著最後期限。國會目前正在研擬一項新的支出法案來資助政府運作。如果無法在 9 月 30 日前達成協議，聯邦政府可能面臨停擺，這將導致許多公共服務中斷。隨著國債達到 40 兆美元且政府接近法定借貸上限，國會議員尋求解決方案的壓力比以往任何時候都大。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To increase in amount or value.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見於描述爬山，這裡用於描述債務數字的增長。文中：The United States has reached a major economic milestone as its national debt climbed past $40 trillion.

keyTerms.definitionEn: The extra money paid for borrowing money.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見於表示「興趣」，這裡指金融上的利息。文中：Today, the government spends more than a trillion dollars every year just to pay the interest on its existing loans.

keyTerms.definitionEn: The financial return or interest rate earned on an investment.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見於農業（產量），這裡指債券的投資報酬率。文中：Investors now demand higher interest rates, known as yields, to lend money to the government.

keyTerms.definitionEn: An event that serves as a warning and makes people realize they need to change their behavior.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 警鐘；提醒人們需要改變現狀的事件。
keyTerms.noteZh: 字面上是「叫醒電話」，這裡比喻為嚴重的警告。文中：Carolyn Bourdeaux of the group Concord Action warned that the current situation should be a wake-up call for leaders in Washington.

quiz.question: According to the article, what is currently the largest expense for the United States federal government?
quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。文章第二段明確指出，政府每年支付的債務利息是聯邦政府的第二大支出，僅次於「社會安全」（Social Security）。選項 A 是第二大支出而非最大。選項 C 是導致債務增加的原因之一，而非政府支出項目。選項 D 是政府稅收來源，而非支出項目。

quiz.question: Based on the information provided, what is a likely consequence if the government fails to manage its growing debt?

options.A: The government will stop collecting import taxes entirely
options.B: The cost of borrowing for individual citizens will likely remain high
options.C: The Treasury Department will stop issuing bonds to investors
options.D: The national debt will automatically decrease due to inflation

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。文章第五段提到政府債券的高利率會連帶提高一般民眾的房貸、車貸及信用卡利率。若債務問題持續，政府需支付更高利息，這將維持高利率環境，影響民眾借貸成本。選項 A 文中未提及。選項 C 不符邏輯，政府仍需透過發債籌資。選項 D 錯誤，通貨膨脹通常會削弱貨幣購買力，而非自動減少債務。

quiz.question: In the final paragraph, what is the meaning of the phrase 'a wake-up call' as used in the context of the debt situation?

options.A: A signal to begin a new government program
options.B: A request for more funding for social services
options.C: A warning that urgent action is needed to address a problem
options.D: A scheduled meeting between political leaders

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。在文中，Carolyn Bourdeaux 使用「a wake-up call」來形容當前的債務危機，意指這是一個警訊，提醒華盛頓的領導人必須正視問題並採取行動，不能再忽視。選項 A、B 與 D 皆偏離了該詞彙在危機情境下作為「警示」的語意。

quiz.question: What is the central message of this article?

options.A: The history of US tax policies over the last twenty years
options.B: The specific impact of Covid-19 relief on the national economy
options.C: The technical process of how the Treasury Department conducts buybacks
options.D: The challenges and concerns surrounding the rapid growth of the US national debt

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 D。整篇文章從債務突破 40 兆美元的里程碑開始，討論了債務增加的原因、對經濟與民眾的影響、專家觀點以及政治上的兩難，核心主題皆圍繞在美國國債快速增長所帶來的嚴峻挑戰。選項 A、B、C 皆僅為文中提到的細節，無法涵蓋全文主旨。
